subject: Performance onboarding: Everline benchmark checklist & prompt set
messages:
From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: marta.lopez@everline.com, devops@everline.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance onboarding: Everline benchmark checklist & prompt set

Hi Marta / Everline team,

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can get a reproducible qualification run scheduled:

Summary of targets we heard on the call:
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 150 ms for short-prompt search-like queries; p50 < 80ms desirable.
- Streaming: first-byte (TTFB) target <= 200 ms for chat flows; steady-state chunk delivery <= 50 ms between chunks.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state tokens/sec target ~1,200 across the pool for your shopping feed workload.
- Concurrency: capability to support up to 60 simultaneous in-flight streaming sessions (50 sustained during peak).

What we'll exchange in this thread (attachments):
- everline-prompt-set-v1.jsonl — representative prompt slices (anonymized), ~300 examples.
- benchmark-harness-specs.pdf — measurement definitions, harness expectations, and run recipe.
- run-config.yaml — sample cluster/run configuration we recommend for parity with our infra.

Key measurement definitions (high-level):
- p50/p95/p99 generation latency: time from HTTP POST accepted to last token emitted (non-streamed).
- streaming TTFB: time from POST to first token byte on the stream (important for UX).
- sustained throughput: average tokens/sec measured over a 10-minute sliding window after warm-up.
- cold vs warm: we will report both cold-start percentiles (first request after model spin-up) and warm (steady-state).

Reproducibility checklist we need from your side:
1) Confirm a test API key or service account with access to the dedicated sandbox endpoint.
2) Confirm which model variant you'll run (model name + exact git/hash or artifact version).
3) Provide a single-run concurrency profile (we suggested a 10m ramp, 30m steady, 10m cool-down).
4) Confirm the time window you can commit for a 6-hour benchmark (we prefer off-peak ops window).

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Everline: confirm service account + run window (Marta)
- Redwood: provide harness artifact + run recipe by EOD (Sergio)
- Redwood: review prompt-set redaction with Everline and finalize v1 (Aditya)

I attached the draft prompt set and the harness spec to this message. If those look good we can lock the run window and I’ll schedule a dedicated engineer to partner with your DevOps during the test.

Thanks — speak soon.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: everline-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (JSONL, 240KB)]
[Attachment: benchmark-harness-specs.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]

From: marta.lopez@everline.com

Cc: devops@everline.com

Subject: Re: Performance onboarding: Everline benchmark checklist & prompt set

Thanks, Sergio — great summary. A few clarifications from our side before we commit a run window: 

1) Data / PII: the prompt set looks anonymized, but can you confirm your recommended redaction steps (token-level vs sample-level)? We need this for compliance.
2) Streaming metrics: do you measure TTFB as the first byte on the connection or the first semantic token? Our client libraries sometimes buffer small frames.
3) Quantization / model parity: we plan to test both fp16 and int8-quant variants. Will Redwood consider those separately in the report?
4) Run window: we can do Thurs 3 Sep 00:00–06:00 UTC assuming no production traffic. Can you confirm Redwood availability for parallel monitoring?

Also share the service account instructions (roles/scopes) — our DevOps prefers to set up a dedicated infra token and limit access.

Cc’ing DevOps so they see the artifacts.

— Marta
Marta Lopez
Senior SRE, Everline Retail
[DevOps: please flag if 00:00–06:00 UTC is a problem]

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: marta.lopez@everline.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance onboarding: Everline benchmark checklist & prompt set

Hi Marta — thanks for the quick read. Answers inline below and a couple of small updates to the harness: 

1) Redaction: we recommend token-level removal for sensitive fields, plus a sampling audit. In practice we provide a redaction checklist in the harness (see section 2.1 of benchmark-harness-specs.pdf). If you prefer, we can run a dry-redaction pass and return an audit log of removed tokens.

2) Streaming TTFB: measurement = first non-empty application token emitted over the HTTP/2 or SSE stream. We exclude connection handshake (TLS) and DNS time — we measure from Redwood ingress receive timestamp. Note: if your client buffers, we’ll capture server-side TTFB and also report client-observed latency so you can compare both.

3) Quantization: yes — please list the exact artifact names you plan to exercise (e.g., model-x_v2_fp16, model-x_v2_int8). We’ll run separate pass(es) and tag results by artifact. Keep in mind int8 may change tail latency behavior; we’ll surface that.

4) Run window: Thurs 3 Sep 00:00–06:00 UTC works for our team. We’ll assign an on-call infra engineer and a solutions lead to be present. 

Reproducibility notes (from our side):
- Seed control: we’ll run deterministic prompt order and persist RNG seeds where applicable; please use the prompt-set order as the canonical sequence.
- Warm-up: harness will do 10 minutes of progressive warm-up at 20% of target concurrency, then ramp to target over 10 minutes.
- KV cache: if you’re running multi-request chains that rely on KV cache reuse, indicate that in the run config so the harness can replicate the cache behavior; otherwise harness assumes independent requests.
- Environment snapshot: we’ll include the model binary checksum, kernel/driver versions, and the runtime config (attached as run-config.yaml).

Attachments included in this message: benchmark-harness-specs.pdf (sections on measurement tables + sample run commands), run-config.yaml (example cluster settings). I also put a live copy of the spec in the shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A7-everline-benchmark/specs

Next steps:
- Marta: confirm exact artifact names and grant a read-only service account to the sandbox endpoint (we provided roles in the harness doc).
- Everline DevOps: confirm the windows and if you want Redwood to initiate the runs or if you’ll run the harness from your side.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for Thurs UTC and include the on-call rotation details.

Cheers,
Sergio
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: benchmark-harness-specs.pdf (PDF, 185KB)]
